claim: A single-Region KMS key generated by AWS KMS is stored and used only in the Region where it was created.
question: Can a single-Region KMS key be used outside the Region where it was created?

values.display: stored and used only in the Region

evidence.quote: A single-Region KMS key generated by AWS KMS is stored and used only in the Region in which it was created.

claim: With AWS KMS multi-Region keys you can replicate a multi-Region primary key into multiple Regions within the same AWS partition.
question: How can one KMS key be used in more than one Region?

evidence.quote: With AWS KMS multi-Region keys you can choose to replicate a multi-Region primary key into multiple Regions within the same AWS partition.

claim: CloudTrail logs show all AWS KMS API requests, both management requests (create, rotate, disable, policy edits) and cryptographic requests (encrypt and decrypt).
question: How can you find out who used or changed a KMS key?

evidence.quote: Logs in AWS CloudTrail will show all AWS KMS API requests, including both management requests (such as create, rotate, disable, policy edits) and cryptographic requests (such as encrypt/decrypt).

claim: Compared with AWS KMS, CloudHSM gives you a validated single-tenant HSM cluster in your VPC, and you have exclusive control over how your keys are used through an authentication mechanism independent from AWS.
question: How does CloudHSM differ from AWS KMS in tenancy and control?

values.display: exclusive control over how your keys are used

evidence.quote: CloudHSM provides you with a validated single-tenant HSM cluster in your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to store and use your keys.
You have exclusive control over how your keys are used through an authentication mechanism independent from AWS.

claim: CloudHSM supports use cases such as DRM, PKI, document signing and cryptographic functions through the PKCS#11, Java JCE or Microsoft CNG interfaces.
question: Which interfaces and use cases point to CloudHSM rather than AWS KMS?

values.display: PKCS#11, Java JCE, or Microsoft CNG interfaces

evidence.quote: You can use CloudHSM to support a variety of use cases, such as Digital Rights Management (DRM), Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), document signing, and cryptographic functions using PKCS#11, Java JCE, or Microsoft CNG interfaces.

claim: AWS KMS manages all your keys centrally, so you can enforce who can use your keys under which conditions, when they get rotated and who can manage them, and audit their use through CloudTrail.
question: What does AWS KMS give you that a CloudHSM cluster does not, in the FAQ comparison?

values.display: Centralized management of all your keys
audit the use of your keys

evidence.quote: Centralized management of all your keys in AWS KMS helps you enforce who can use your keys under which conditions, when they get rotated, and who can manage them.
AWS KMS integration with CloudTrail gives you the ability to audit the use of your keys to support your regulatory and compliance activities.

claim: AWS KMS charges for every KMS key you create and for API requests each month above a free tier, with no minimum fee and no setup fees.
question: What do you pay for in AWS KMS?

evidence.quote: You are charged for all KMS keys you create and for API requests made to the service each month above a free tier.
With AWS KMS, you pay only for what you use; there is no minimum fee.

claim: AWS managed KMS keys that AWS services create on your behalf are free to store in your account.
question: Do you pay to store AWS managed KMS keys?

values.display: free to store in your account

evidence.quote: AWS managed AWS KMS keys that are created on your behalf by AWS services are free to store in your account.

claim: API requests that involve asymmetric KMS keys, and requests to GenerateDataKeyPair and GenerateDataKeyPairWithoutPlaintext, are excluded from the KMS free tier.
question: Which KMS requests are not covered by the free tier?

values.display: API requests involving asymmetric KMS keys

evidence.quote: *API requests involving asymmetric KMS keys and API requests to the GenerateDataKeyPair and GenerateDataKeyPairWithoutPlaintext APIs are excluded from the Free Tier.

claim: You can import a copy of your key from your own key management infrastructure into AWS KMS and use it with any integrated AWS service or in your own applications.
question: Can you bring your own key material to AWS KMS?

values.display: import a copy of your key

evidence.quote: You can import a copy of your key from your own key management infrastructure to AWS KMS and use it with any integrated AWS service or from within your own applications.

claim: Imported keys help meet compliance requirements such as generating or keeping a secure copy of the key in your own infrastructure and being able to delete the imported copy from AWS immediately.
question: When would you use imported key material in AWS KMS?

values.display: immediately delete the imported copy of the key

evidence.quote: Imported keys are designed to help you meet your compliance requirements which may include the ability to generate or maintain a secure copy of the key in your infrastructure, and the ability to immediately delete the imported copy of the key from AWS infrastructure.

claim: You can import symmetric keys, asymmetric keys (RSA and elliptic curve) and HMAC keys into AWS KMS.
question: Which key types can you import into AWS KMS?

evidence.quote: You can import symmetric keys, asymmetric keys (RSA and elliptic curve), and HMAC keys.

note: Import of asymmetric and HMAC key material was added after mid-2022 (numbers+changes lens dates it).

claim: During import, your key must be wrapped by a public key that AWS KMS provides, using a supported wrapping algorithm, so that only AWS KMS can decrypt it.
question: How is key material protected in transit when you import it into AWS KMS?

values.display: wrapped by an AWS KMS-provided public key

evidence.quote: During the import process, your key must be wrapped by an AWS KMS-provided public key using the supported wrapping algorithm.

claim: For imported keys you are responsible for keeping a copy in your own key management infrastructure so you can re-import them; for keys generated by AWS KMS, AWS ensures availability, security and durability until you schedule deletion.
question: Who is responsible for the durability of imported key material?

values.display: responsible for maintaining a copy of your imported keys

evidence.quote: You are responsible for maintaining a copy of your imported keys in your key management infrastructure so that you can re-import them at any time.
AWS, however, verifies the availability, security, and durability of keys generated by AWS KMS on your behalf until you schedule the keys for deletion.

claim: Keys generated by AWS KMS have no expiration time and cannot be deleted immediately; there is a mandatory 7 to 30 day wait period.
question: Can a KMS key whose material AWS KMS generated be deleted immediately?

qualifiers.scope: per KMS key with key material generated by AWS KMS
qualifiers.condition: contrast: imported key material can be deleted on demand

evidence.quote: Keys generated by AWS KMS do not have an expiration time and cannot be deleted immediately; there is a mandatory 7 to 30 day wait period.

claim: If imported key material expired or was deleted, you can re-import your copy of it, with a valid expiration period, under the original KMS key.
question: What can you do when imported key material has expired or was deleted by accident?

values.display: re-import your copy of the key material

evidence.quote: You can re-import your copy of the key material with a valid expiration period to AWS KMS under the original AWS KMS key so it can be used.

claim: After you import key material, a CloudWatch metric counts down the time to expiration every few minutes, and a CloudWatch event is sent when the imported key expires.
question: How can you be alerted before imported key material expires?

values.display: counts down the time to expiration

evidence.quote: Once you import your key to an AWS KMS key, you will receive a CloudWatch Metric every few minutes that counts down the time to expiration of the imported key.
You will also receive a CloudWatch Event once the imported key under your AWS KMS key expires.

claim: AWS KMS creates 256-bit symmetric KMS keys for encryption, and when it uses one to encrypt or decrypt it uses AES in Galois Counter Mode (AES-GCM).
question: What key size and algorithm do symmetric KMS keys use?

evidence.quote: AWS KMS supports 256-bit keys when creating a KMS key for encryption and decryption.
When AWS KMS uses a 256-bit KMS key on your behalf to encrypt or decrypt, the AES algorithm in Galois Counter Mode (AES-GCM) is used.

claim: Encryption algorithms cannot be used with the elliptic curve KMS key types; the RSAES_OAEP encryption algorithms work with the RSA key types.
question: Can an elliptic curve KMS key encrypt data?

evidence.quote: Encryption algorithms cannot be used with the elliptic curve key types (ECC NIST P-256, ECC NIST P-384, ECC NIST-521, and ECC SECG P-256k1).

claim: Data sent to AWS KMS for asymmetric operations is limited to 4 KB; data for Encrypt, Decrypt or Re-Encrypt with asymmetric operations must be less than 4 KB.
question: What is the size limit for data sent to AWS KMS for asymmetric operations?

evidence.quote: The size limit is 4 KB.
Any data submitted to the Encrypt, Decrypt, or Re-Encrypt APIs that require use of asymmetric operations must also be less than 4 KB.
